research_question: Does a matched two-stage DenseNet-201 hierarchy improve final three-class validation performance by separating Normal/Pneumonia recognition from Viral/Bacterial etiology?
stage1_training_scope: All locked-manifest training rows; Normal=0 and Viral/Bacterial together=Pneumonia=1.
stage2_training_scope: Only locked-manifest Viral and Bacterial training rows; Normal rows are excluded from Stage 2 optimization.
combined_validation_scope: All 874 locked-validation rows. Both stages infer every row so soft probabilities can be composed without hard-routing bias.

probability_rule.normalization: The three products must already sum to one within absolute tolerance 0.000001; post-hoc renormalization is prohibited.

isolation_rule: The two stages differ only in task_mode, class_names, and run_id. Architecture, initialization source, preprocessing, augmentation, optimizer, scheduler, loss, resolution, batch size, epoch budget, seed, and manifests are matched.

seed42_advancement_gate.primary: combined validation macro F1 must be at least FT-REF plus 0.005 absolute
seed42_advancement_gate.purpose: Authorize seeds 123 and 2026 only; passing does not authorize locked-test access.

final_claim_gate.purpose: Only a completed multi-seed comparison may support a best-confirmed-system claim.

failure_behavior: Do not evaluate the hierarchy if either stage lacks a completed best checkpoint.
Fail on configuration drift, checkpoint hash mismatch, non-finite probabilities, probability rows that do not sum to one, or validation-path misalignment.
Do not substitute the locked test for validation and do not generate locked-test predictions.
If the seed-42 advancement gate fails, stop FT-009B without seeds 123 or 2026.
